questions.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ 5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 7 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $v$ and $w$ are orthogonal. Find $(u+9v)\cdot w+v\cdot (u+7w).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $v$ and $w$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $v\cdot w=0.$ Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(u+9v)\cdot w+v\cdot (u+7w) & =u\cdot w+(9v)\cdot w+v\cdot u+v\cdot (7w) \\  & =u\cdot w+9(v\cdot w)+v\cdot u+7(v\cdot w) \\  & =u\cdot w+9\cdot 0+v\cdot u+7\cdot 0 \\  & =u\cdot w+v\cdot u \\  & =(4\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-5)+1\cdot 7+(-3)\cdot (-3)) \\  & +((-4)\cdot 4+3\cdot (-2)+5\cdot 1+4\cdot (-3)) \\  & =(8+10+7+9)+(-16-6+5-12) \\  & =34-29 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: If $u=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 2k \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and $v=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 4 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal vectors, then $k=$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $u⊥v$, they are orthogonal vectors, we have that their dot product is equal to zero.
First, let's calculate the dot product in terms of $k$:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =1\cdot (-5)+(-3)\cdot 1+2k\cdot 4+(-2)\cdot k \\  & =-5-3+8k-2k \\  & =6k-8\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the dot product to zero, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}6k-8 & =0 \\ 6k & =8 \\ k & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}a \\ -1 \\ b \\ 2\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ -2 \\ 5\end{aligned}],$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u$ is orthogonal to $v$ and $w.$ What is the value of $a-b?$
questions.worked_solution:
Given that $u$ is orthogonal to $v$ and $w$, we have

$$
\{\begin{aligned}u\cdot v=0 \\ u\cdot w=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's consider the first equation $u\cdot v=0.$ Calculating the dot product in terms of $a$ and $b$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & =0 \\ a\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 4+b\cdot (-2)+2\cdot 5 & =0 \\ 2a-4-2b+10 & =0 \\ 2a-2b & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, for the second equation $u\cdot w=0$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot w & =0 \\ a\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-3)+b\cdot 1+2\cdot (-3) & =0 \\ a+3+b-6 & =0 \\ a+b & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the values of $a$ and $b$, we need to solve the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2a-2b=-6 \\ a+b=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second equation by $-2$ and adding the result to the first equation, we obtain

$$
-4b=-12\,⟹\,b=3.
$$

Substituting $b=3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2a-2(3) & =-6 \\ 2a-6 & =-6 \\ 2a & =0 \\ a & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have that

$$
a-b=0-3=-3.
$$

questions.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ k \\ k \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ and $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -k-1 \\ -7 \\ -12\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that  $u⊥v.$ Find the value of $k.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that their dot product is equal to zero.
First, let's calculate the dot product in terms of $k$:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =7\cdot 3+k\cdot (-k-1)+k\cdot (-7)+3\cdot (-12) \\  & =21-{k}^{2}-k-7k-36 \\  & =-{k}^{2}-8k-15 \\  & =-({k}^{2}+8k+15)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the dot product to zero, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-({k}^{2}+8k+15) & =0 \\ -(k+5)(k+3) & =0 \\ k & =-5,-3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ 7 \\ 5\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u\,⊥\,v.$ Find $(u-2v)\cdot (v+2w).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $u\cdot v=0.$ Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(u-2v)\cdot (v+2w) & =u\cdot v-2(v\cdot v)+2(u\cdot w)-4(v\cdot w) \\  & =0-2(v\cdot v)+2(u\cdot w)-4(v\cdot w) \\  & =-2(3\cdot 3+2\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-2)+2\cdot 2) \\  & +2((-2)\cdot 0+5\cdot 2+7\cdot 0+5\cdot (-3)) \\  & -4(3\cdot 0+2\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot 0+2\cdot (-3)) \\  & =-2(21)+2(-5)-4(-2) \\  & =-42-10+8 \\  & =-44.\end{aligned}
$$
